title: Dashboard concision and trace anchoring cookbook
body:
Context and intent:
This is a compact working cookbook to help the observability team AND consuming product teams prune dashboards aggressively, anchor traces to investigative entry points, and keep metric definitions tight. The tone here is practical: concrete heuristics, short snippets, and a small experiment log so we can iterate fast.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Dashboards have ballooned: panels duplicated across orgs, high-cardinality queries cost a lot, and oncall noise is increasing.
- Traces are collected inconsistently; investigators spend time mapping which trace spans actually matter for token-serving and caching issues.
- We need a lightweight spec that non-observability engineers can use when requesting dashboard panels or traces for a rollout.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce dashboard panel count by 30% on the top 20 dashboards by query-cost within Q2.
- Ensure every alerting panel has a linked trace anchor and a reproducible probe within 24h of oncall ticket creation.
- Add metadata to panels: owner, query-cost-estimate, trace-anchor-id, last-validated.

Quick rules for concision (panel hygiene):
1) Panel budget: 8 panels per dashboard as a default cap. Exceptions require a short PR and an owner.
2) Duplicate elimination: If panel A is a filtered view of panel B (same metric + filter subset), delete A or convert to a template/variable-driven control.
3) Card max-cardinality: avoid unbounded group_bys; use top-k + others bucket. If more than 5 unique group keys expected, replace with heatmap or cohort summary.
4) Query cost flagging: panels with 95th percentile query runtime > 500ms get flagged for optimization.
5) Owner and SLT: every panel must declare an owner and a simple SLT (e.g., SLO: p99 < 150ms).

Metric definition checklist (what "counts"):
- request.count: total user-facing inference requests received by front proxy (tagged: route, model, customer_tier). Unit: requests. Aggregation: sum per minute.
- token.generated: tokens emitted by model runtime (tags: model_version, quant_profile). Unit: tokens. Aggregation: sum per minute.
- kv.cache.hit_rate: percent of prefix/KV hits at runtime (tags: model, tenant_isolation). Unit: percent. Aggregation: weighted average.
- runtime.tok_latency: time per token in ms broken into phases (attention, matmul, kernel-switch). If instrumentation missing, fall back to per-inference time.
- queue.backlog: number of pending inference calls waiting for a GPU slot or runtime worker. Use max over 1m window.
- error.rate: user visible errors (4xx/5xx) annotated with error.kind (timeout, oom, bad_request).

A note on cardinality and privacy: do not include raw user ids or full prompt strings in metrics. Use hashed identifiers (tenant_hash) and cohort tags. For PHI-sensitive customers use separate private telemetry (see privacy playbook).

Trace anchoring: what to include and why
- Anchor concept: a small canonical span or trace that represents the investigative entrypoint for a class of problems. Examples:
  * "frontend.request" span: capture route, client-region, request_size. This is the top-level anchor for request-level latency.
  * "runtime.kv_lookup" span: shows KV cache hit/miss and duration; critical for cold-cache investigations.
  * "gpu.scheduler.enqueue" span: helpful when queue.backlog rises.
- Trace tags to standardize: trace_anchored=true, ticket_id (if linked), run_id, model_variant, tenant_hash.
- Minimal span payload: span name, start_ms, duration_ms, status, key tags (see above), and an abbreviated debug snippet (<= 256 chars) when relevant.

Anchoring heuristics (how to pick anchors):
1) pick the entrypoint most likely to change during the incident (e.g., cache hit behavior when rollout changes).
2) prefer a span with stable instrumentation across models (frontend.request or runtime.scheduler).
3) for model-quality incidents include generation.output_length and model.temperature tags on anchor.

Dashboard integration: manifest fields to add to panel JSON
- owner: alias or email
- query_cost_estimate: low|medium|high (based on historical runtime and cardinality)
- trace_anchor: canonical span name or trace pattern (e.g., runtime.kv_lookup)
- last_validated: YYYY-MM-DD
- validation_notes: short freeform text

Trace-driven alert design (quick pattern):
- Alert rule: increase in runtime.tok_latency.p99 by > 2x for 5min AND concurrent increase in queue.backlog > 20 -> severity P1 and capture 1 sample trace per minute for 10 minutes tagged with trace_anchored=true.
- On alert fire: run the probe that reproduces the synthetic trace, attach run_id to the incident.

Small experiment log (what we tried recently):
- 2026-01-15: Converted top-5 latency dashboards to 8-panel cap and introduced owner metadata. Result: query-cost decreased ~18% on those dashboards; non-owner panels reappeared -> next step: enforce through dashboard PR check.
- 2026-01-28: Introduced runtime.kv_lookup anchor in canary traces for a dedicated model rollout (canary-v3). Result: faster triage; median time to identify cache-miss root cause dropped from 47m -> 12m.
- 2026-02-20: Trialed dynamic top-k groupings for tenant panels (top 10 + other). Saved query cost but ops wanted per-tenant breakdown for top customers; resolution: allow per-tenant detailed dashboards behind a gate and with cost-alloc tags.

Requests / PR recipe for teams (how to ask for new panels or trace spans)
1) Open a small dashboard PR in obs-dashboards with: intent paragraph, panel json, owner, query_cost_estimate.
2) Include a sample trace pattern or suggested anchor span.
3) Add validation checklist: how to reproduce, what signal validates the panel (metric id and expected behavior).
4) Tag the obs-owner and request a 48h review.

Oncall play for missing anchors:
- If an oncall ticket arrives and the alerting panel lacks a trace_anchor: immediate triage step is to run the synthetic probe (if exists) and create a short trace sample, then update the panel with trace_anchor and last_validated. Create JIRA-ENGOBS-XXX for any panels that cannot be anchored within the shift.

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve:
- What is the enforcement mechanism for the 8-panel cap? (policy vs CI check) -> action: Diego to prototype dashboard-lint CI by 2026-03-12.
- How do we quantify query-cost consistently across Grafana/other tooling? Need a standard query-cost model. -> action: Sofia to draft cost model.
- Sampling budget vs investigator needs: how many anchored traces to retain in hot storage? Current storage costs are opaque.

Next immediate actions (owners assigned):
- Add owner/query_cost_estimate/trace_anchor fields to dashboard templates (Evan Brooks) - due 2026-03-09.
- Dashboard-lint prototype (Diego Morales) - due 2026-03-12.
- Cost model draft for query_cost_estimate (Sofia Ivanova) - due 2026-03-18.
- Run a surgery session with two product teams to prune their dashboards (Asha) - schedule by 2026-03-05.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this short; link to broader obs governance page for policy text.
- When in doubt, recommend removing the panel and asking for it back via PR if someone needs it. Better: fewer but trusted owner-driven panels.

References and helpful links:
- Confluence governance (see linked_artifacts)
- Slack channel: #obs-dashboard-prs
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-dashboards/pull/128

If you are reading this and want to help: pick an ownerless dashboard and prune one panel. Small wins add up.

-- Asha
